record.paper_title: Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives on Open Problems
record.context_brief: Theory comparing offline model-based and dynamic-programming methods
record.original_question: Under nonlinear function approximation, can offline model-based reinforcement learning theoretically improve over offline model-free dynamic-programming methods, and what theoretical bounds characterize the optimal performance achievable by offline model-based reinforcement learning compared with offline dynamic programming? The question concerns whether learning future-state predictors yields fundamental advantages over predicting returns when both approaches are trained from the same fixed offline data.

evidence.quote: It is also still an open theoretical question as to whether model-based RL methods even in theory can improve over model-free dynamic programming algorithms. The reasoning behind this question is that, although dynamic programming methods do not explicitly learn a model, they essentially utilize the dataset as a “non-parametric” model. Fundamentally, both dynamic programming methods and model-based RL methods are solving prediction problems, with the former predicting future returns, and the latter predicting future states.

In the linear function approximation case, it is known that model-based updates and fitted value iteration updates actually produce identical iterates (Vanseijen and Sutton, 2015; Parr et al., 2008), though it is unknown whether this relationship holds under non-linear function approximation. Therefore, exploring the theoretical bounds on the optimal performance of offline model-based RL methods under non-linear function approximation, as compared to offline dynamic programming methods, remains an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a discounted Markov decision process (MDP) M = (S, A, P, r, γ) with state space S, action space A, transition kernel P(s'|s,a), reward function r(s,a) ∈ [0,1], and discount factor γ ∈ [0,1). Suppose we are given a fixed offline dataset D = {(s_i, a_i, r_i, s'_i)}_{i=1}^n drawn i.i.d. from some behavior distribution μ over S × A, with s'_i ∼ P(·|s_i, a_i). Let F be a parametric (in general nonlinear) function-approximation class.

Consider two families of offline algorithms that use only D and the class F:
(1) Offline model-free dynamic programming methods (e.g. fitted value iteration / fitted Q-iteration), which iteratively fit a value or Q-function f ∈ F by regressing toward the empirical Bellman targets r_i + γ max_{a'} f(s'_i, a').
(2) Offline model-based methods, which fit a transition (and reward) model P̂, r̂ from F (or a related class) to the data and then plan in the resulting estimated MDP.

It is known that under linear function approximation (with a fixed linear feature map and standard least-squares fits) the iterates produced by model-based value iteration and by least-squares fitted value iteration coincide.

Question: Under nonlinear function approximation, can offline model-based reinforcement learning theoretically outperform offline model-free dynamic programming when both methods are restricted to the same fixed dataset D and the same (or comparable) function class F? Specifically, establish — or refute — sample-complexity and suboptimality bounds on the value of the policy returned by offline model-based RL relative to the optimal policy that quantify any provable advantage (or equivalence) over the bounds achievable by offline dynamic programming methods, under standard assumptions on data coverage (e.g. concentrability) and approximation-class expressivity.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is described as an open theoretical question about whether offline model-based RL can provably improve over offline model-free dynamic programming under nonlinear function approximation. While there has been substantial subsequent work on offline RL theory (e.g., pessimism-based bounds for both model-free and model-based methods, and equivalence results in the linear setting), no general result is known that settles whether model-based offline RL has a fundamental theoretical advantage over fitted value iteration / FQI under nonlinear approximation when given the same data and comparable function classes. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: It is also still an open theoretical question as to whether model-based RL methods even in theory can improve over model-free dynamic programming algorithms... exploring the theoretical bounds on the optimal performance of offline model-based RL methods under non-linear function approximation, as compared to offline dynamic programming methods, remains an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The question is stated as an open theoretical problem, with the linear-case equivalence known but the nonlinear case unresolved.
